s: Which of the following policy is currently followed by India with regard to determination of the amount of fertilizer subsidy?

s: On which category of fertilizer, the government provides the highest subsidy?

s: Why does the Government of India promote the use of 'Neem-coated Urea' in agriculture?
o: Release of Neem oil in the soil increases nitrogen fixation by the soil microorganisms.
Neem coating slows down the rate of distribution of urea in the soil
Nitrous oxide, which is a greenhouse gas, is not at all released into the atmosphere by crop fields.
It is a combination of a weedicide and a fertilizer for particular crops.
x: Neem coating slows the dissolution and nitrogen release of urea in the soil, cutting losses; it does not add nitrogen fixation, stop all N2O or act as a weedicide.

s: The use of balanced fertiliser use is most desirable because it
x: Balanced fertilisation supplies nutrients in the right proportion as per soil test, so it corrects all deficiencies, rather than merely adding NPK.

s: The percentage of nitrogen in urea is
x: Urea contains about 46% nitrogen; 47% is the nearest option, the others are far off.

s: Efficient fertilisers use results in
x: Efficient fertiliser use means higher nutrient-use efficiency, i.e. more crop produced per kg of fertiliser.

s: The urea briquettes are used as a form of nitrogenous fertiliser. This is because of which of the following reason?
o: Urea/nitrogen is highly volatile in nature and is lost immediately
Urea is highly soluble in water
x: Urea dissolves easily and loses nitrogen through volatilisation and leaching, so slow-release briquettes are placed deep in the soil; all the reasons apply.

s: The two largest consumers of chemical fertilizers in India are

s: An ammonium compound used as a fertiliser
x:
Official key: ammonium phosphate. Strictly, ammonium sulphate is also a fertiliser (PMF Environment 07 p.2-3: nitrogenous – ammonium sulphate; phosphatic – ammonium phosphate).
Ammonium phosphate (DAP/MAP) is a widely used fertiliser and is the key; ammonium sulphate is also a nitrogenous fertiliser, so the stem is loose. Ammonium carbonate and chloride are not standard fertilisers.

s:

I. Fixing minimum support price for agricultural produce of all crops.

II. Computerisation of primary agricultural credit societies.

III. Social capital development.

IV. Free electricity supply to farmers.

V. Waiver of agricultural loans by the banking system.

What is true about the Second Green Revolution in India?

II. It aims at extending seed-water- fertiliser technology to areas which hitherto could not benefit from green revolution.

III. The 'Reduction Commitments' are expressed in terms of a "Total Aggregate Measurement of Support" which includes all product-specific support and non-product-specific support in one single figure.

II. Public sector impact via changes in government expenditure/taxes.

III. Crowding-out impact via higher borrowings by State Governments.

IV. Crowding-in impact via higher credit availability as bank NPAs fall.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: A farm-loan waiver acts on aggregate demand through all four channels: private consumption, public-sector spending/taxes, crowding-out by higher State borrowing and crowding-in as bank NPAs fall.
